transcript.text: Talk about the circumstances, Tom. She was on the pier on the lake front in Michigan with some of her friends going to see the northern lights. And there's a lighthouse at the end of the pier. Can you explain to everyone who you're understanding of what happened? I understand that Sheridan was the first one walking out in that pier some distance ahead of everyone else. And she got to the end, went around the corner of the lighthouse, and saw a man in a mask holding a gun. She turned around quickly, warned her friends there's a man with a gun run. And she made it about 40 feet, and she was shot in the back. Shot in the back. I don't understand what kind of person could shoot a child in the back as they're running away. I don't know where that comes from. It's a depravity. When you asked who we were in the courthouse, he didn't look at us. I don't know if I wanted him to look at me, but he didn't look at us. At one point, I did see his face. He turned presumably to see if someone was in the courthouse for him. We were surrounded by 30 of our best friends and family who had journeyed to Chicago with us. We had our family with them. And no one was there for him. But when he did turn to the side, I saw his eyes, and they were cold. I feared at that moment that there was never going to be any justice that he would have, would never take away or could never supersede the loss that we've had. I don't feel like he would ever feel the level of loss. We want what that justice looks like.
